title: Pet owners say smart pet feeder outage led to furry ones going unfed
gist: A roughly 38-hour Petlibro cloud outage starting Tuesday 5 am PT left users unable to control smart pet feeders, and multiple owners reported scheduled feedings that were skipped, partial or late — directly contradicting Petlibro's product-page claims that schedules run locally on-device during network failures.

themes.theme: The outage timeline and data loss

insights.claim: Petlibro's cloud outage began Tuesday at 5 am PT with the company acknowledging a service disruption affecting app access and remote device control, and was declared fully restored only at 7 pm PT Wednesday — roughly 38 hours.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A day-and-a-half outage on a device with a safety-critical function is the kind of incident that drives regulatory attention to IoT reliability disclosure.
insights.locator: Petlibro first acknowledged problems on Tuesday

insights.claim: Petlibro CEO York Wu attributed the outage to how the Petlibro app communicates with devices through its online servers, locating the fault in cloud connectivity rather than the devices themselves.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Cloud-dependency is the single point of failure across the connected-device category — architecture, not hardware quality, determines outage blast radius.
insights.quote: related to how the Petlibro app communicates with devices through its online servers
insights.locator: In a statement to The Verge

insights.claim: Petlibro warned that records generated during the disruption may be permanently unrecoverable, including device operation history, feeding and litter box records, notifications, cloud-stored videos and highlight videos.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Permanent data loss during an outage undermines the recurring-subscription value proposition that cloud pet-tech vendors monetize.
insights.quote: Certain records generated during the disruption may not be recoverable, including some device operation history, feeding or litter box records, notifications, cloud-stored videos, and highlight videos.
insights.locator: The page also notes that previously saved schedules

insights.claim: Some Reddit users reported still experiencing problems the morning after Petlibro declared services fully restored, and app-connection-dependent features such as the 'Feed Now' button may remain disrupted per CEO York Wu.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Divergence between vendor status pages and user experience is a reliability-reporting credibility issue that scales with installed base.

themes.theme: Marketing claims vs. observed device behavior

insights.claim: Petlibro's Granary 2 product page states that if the feeder goes offline, feeding schedules will continue to run automatically and the device can still perform pet recognition and automatic lid operation locally, and the One RFID page says scheduled meals continue during network errors.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Explicit offline-operation claims on product pages create a consumer-protection exposure if devices demonstrably fail that way.
insights.quote: If the feeder goes offline, remote control through the app will be unavailable, but feeding schedules will continue to run automatically.
insights.locator: Petlibro claims that at least some of its feeders

insights.claim: Users reported three distinct failure modes during the outage — devices performing no scheduled feedings at all, performing some but not others, and performing feedings late — directly contradicting the offline-autonomy claim.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Partial, inconsistent failure is harder to detect and remediate than total failure, making the reliability problem worse than a clean outage.
insights.quote: various users online claimed that during the outage, their devices did not perform any scheduled feedings, performed some feedings but not others, or performed feedings late
insights.locator: Some user reports have also conflicted

insights.claim: Wu maintained that scheduled feedings are programmed directly onto the device and should run without an internet command, while conceding Petlibro is aware of reports from customers whose devices did not behave as expected and is reviewing those cases individually.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Case-by-case review rather than a systemic acknowledgment is the standard vendor posture that delays recall or remediation decisions.
insights.locator: In response to claims that feeders did not perform

insights.claim: The author hypothesizes that a firmware or software problem triggered by the cloud outage prevented locally stored schedules from executing, since the schedules are supposed to be device-resident — though user error remains a possibility.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: If cloud failures can cascade into local firmware failure, 'works offline' claims across the entire IoT category are weaker than they appear.
insights.locator: Considering that scheduled feedings are supposed to be stored

themes.theme: Trust erosion in smart devices for critical tasks

insights.claim: Some users reported receiving no email notification about the outage and being unaware their pet had gone unfed for hours, meaning the failure was silent from the owner's perspective.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Absence of out-of-band failure notification is a design gap that turns a service outage into an undetected safety incident.
insights.locator: Some users online reported not receiving an email

insights.claim: Customer trust damage is immediate and behavioral, with one user stating they have lost trust but lack time to find an alternative before upcoming travel and cannot arrange five daily in-person feedings.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: High switching friction retains customers short-term but converts them into churn candidates at the next purchase cycle.
insights.quote: I've lost trust and don't have time to find a new solution for upcoming travel. I have someone coming for check-ins, but they can't come in 5 times every day to give food
insights.locator: Some users online reported not receiving an email

insights.claim: The incident makes the case that dumb automatic feeders can outperform smart ones for critical tasks, since cloud dependency introduces failure modes that mechanical timers do not have.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A reusable lens for evaluating connected-hardware categories: added connectivity must clear the reliability bar of the dumb alternative, not just add features.
insights.quote: Petlibro's situation can make dumb automatic feeders look smart.
insights.locator: Although companion apps, when they work
